page.description: A challenging multiple-choice question set in biology, chemistry, and physics, authored by PhD-level experts.
Expert-written math problems covering advanced undergrad through early career research.
Exceptionally difficult research-level math problems.
The hardest tier of problems from the MATH dataset, drawn from competitions like the AMC 10, AMC 12, and AIME.
45 competition-style math problems from OTIS, harder than MATH Level 5 but easier than FrontierMath.

GitHub issues from real-world Python repos, testing whether models can implement valid code fixes.
Note: our SWE-bench Verified scaffold was significantly upgraded in February 2026.
1,000 factual questions about politics, science and technology, art, sports, geography, music, and more.
100 novel puzzles, generated programmatically with a chess engine. Each puzzle has a single best next move.
A test of AI systems' learning capabilities, measuring whether their scores improve across repeated playthroughs of the relatively obscure game Earthborne Rangers.
100 positions from a puzzle-oriented variant of a well-known game, the details of which are deliberately left undisclosed.
A long-horizon coding benchmark. Models reimplement entire programs end-to-end, without access to the original source code.
A benchmark that evaluates models’ performance on a set of challenging programming problems from Exercism, an online programming education platform.
A concept-learning benchmark that evaluates few-shot abstraction, pattern induction, and program-like reasoning from input–output examples.
A multiple-choice science benchmark assessing grade-school science knowledge and reasoning on questions from the AI2 ARC dataset.
A benchmark which evaluates models on their ability to play a series of games with widely varying difficulties.
A curated subset of BIG-bench tasks that remain difficult for large language models, probing compositional, symbolic, and multi-step reasoning.
A cybersecurity agent benchmark measuring autonomous vulnerability discovery and exploitation across sandboxed challenges.
A benchmark testing models’ ability to identify the real world location a picture was taken at, based on the popular game [GeoGuessr](https://www.geoguessr.com/).
A grade-school math word problem benchmark focused on multi-step arithmetic reasoning and exact-match solutions.
A long-context language modeling benchmark where the final word of a passage must be predicted from broader discourse.

A creative story-writing benchmark where models must weave ten assigned elements into short stories, graded on a 0–10 rubric by a panel of LLM judges. Frozen at the benchmark's final 0–10 leaderboard (August 2025).
A multi-task exam-style benchmark covering dozens of academic and professional subjects to test breadth of knowledge and problem solving.
A physical commonsense benchmark where models choose the more feasible solution to everyday problems.
A benchmark testing common-sense reasoning including ‘trick questions’ and situations that require an understanding of space, time or social cues.
A suite of diverse language understanding tasks designed to be more challenging than GLUE, emphasizing reasoning and sample efficiency.
A benchmark of tasks which require a model to complete tasks using a computer terminal, testing its ability to understand and employ the programs available to it.
A community-run evaluation of end-to-end software agents that attempt realistic tasks in reproducible environments.
A series of questions testing models’ ability to comprehend diagrams depicting simple scenarios involving balls falling down a series of ramps and landing in buckets.
A benchmark of nonstandard ML engineering tasks in a variety of domains.
A benchmark evaluating whether AI agents can execute long-horizon professional tasks in investment banking, management consulting, and corporate law within realistic simulated work environments.
A harder successor to ARC-AGI that tests few-shot abstract reasoning and pattern generalization on grid-based tasks, with an added emphasis on efficiency of compute per task solved.
A set of 2,500 expert-authored questions spanning over 100 academic subjects, designed to test the limits of frontier AI models on problems that require deep, specialized knowledge.
A benchmark scoring coding agents on ambiguous, multi-file tasks drawn from real Cursor sessions.
A long-horizon software engineering benchmark tasking AI coding agents with implementing a Game Boy Advance emulator from scratch.
A benchmark testing whether AI can reason through complex, open-ended, research-level physics problems modeled on entry-level original research projects.
A benchmark measuring how far LLM agents can climb a "capability ladder" of software exploitation against real, hardened security vulnerabilities.
A benchmark measuring model performance on well-specified tasks drawn from selected real-world occupations.
A benchmark testing whether models can learn genuinely new knowledge from context at inference time and then apply it to expert-designed tasks.
A companion to CL-bench testing whether models can learn from and reason over messy, real-life context such as everyday communication, scattered notes, and behavioral traces.
An agentic benchmark testing whether LLMs can write Surface Evolver simulations of liquid surfaces shaped by surface tension.
Durations of the longest task that models can complete correctly more often than not, across a set of software engineering and related tasks.
A benchmark of original, long-horizon software engineering tasks written from scratch across active open-source repositories.
A benchmark of graduate-level mathematics problems where models must write Lean 4 proofs that pass formal verification.
A benchmark testing whether coding agents can produce mergeable fixes for real, hard open-source issues.
A benchmark measuring how well models judge the quality of conceptual arguments, scored by agreement with expert ratings.
A benchmark of handcrafted multiple-choice questions testing models' understanding of the decision theory of Newcomb-like problems.
A dynamic, continuously updated benchmark of AI forecasting ability on real-world future events, with direct comparison to human superforecasters and the general public.
A collection of problems posed or studied by mathematician Paul Erdős, open as of August 2026 and curated to be especially interesting and difficult.
A test of spatial reasoning. Models are shown photos of IKEA furniture builds, some with deliberate assembly mistakes, and must say whether the build is correct and identify the mistaken step.
A benchmark testing whether models can answer questions about real-world professional PDFs.
An ultra-long-horizon software engineering benchmark testing coding agents on implementation, performance, scientific-computing, visual-reasoning and AI-research tasks with a 20-hour budget per task.
A scientist-curated benchmark of research-coding problems drawn from across the natural sciences.

A platform where users vote on which of two anonymous models do a better job producing websites according to the user’s requests. Previously known as WebDev Arena, now a subset of [Text Arena](https://arena.ai/leaderboard/text).
A spatial-intelligence benchmark where AI agents convert apartment photographs into 2D floor plans.
A benchmark testing whether vision-language models can build spatial mental models of scenes from limited camera views.
A benchmark of programmatically generated spatial visualization puzzles for multimodal models, spanning mental rotation, folding, penetration, and animation.
A "pastcasting" benchmark where forecasting agents research already-resolved questions against a frozen web snapshot, scored on the Brier scale.
A benchmark of long, multimodal puzzle-hunt puzzles requiring creative multi-step reasoning over mixed text and images.
A benchmark testing whether language models can write code that runs faster than expert reference implementations while remaining correct.
A benchmark evaluating AI on long-horizon, objective-driven algorithm engineering using hard combinatorial optimization problems from competitive programming contests.
A benchmark measuring an AI agent's ability to stay coherent and run a simulated vending machine business profitably over a full simulated year.
An agentic benchmark of 11 hand-made machine learning and data analysis tasks with unfamiliar data, unspecified goals, and limited feedback.
Models play both Slay the Spire games at their respective maximum difficulties through a computer-use harness.
